scope: Theorem 4.1 (Birational constancy over a curve) of the manuscript “Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation” (preprints/Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b1b750b309e5c5a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let π◦ : P◦ → C◦ be a smooth projective morphism with connected fibers, where C◦ is a smooth connected complex algebraic curve. Suppose that its very general fiber D satisfies κ(D) = 0, h0 (D, KD) = 1. Put n = dim D and assume that the entire top Hodge bundle Fn(Rnπ◦ ∗C⊗OC◦ ) is a flat line with finite monodromy character. Then there are a finite extension L/C(C◦) and a smooth connected projective variety D0/C such that the generic fiber after extension to L is birational to (D0)L. If a finite group Γ acts on P◦ over C◦, one can choose D0 with a Γ-action and choose this bi- rational identification Γ-equivariantly. The same conclusion holds for a finite fiberwise birational action, after replacing the family by an equivariant smooth projective model.
